captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/19_byol, specifically its ResNet-50 path (models/resnet50_byol.py, data/byol_dataset.py, train_pretrain_resnet50.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Grill et al. (2020) BYOL, torch/torchvision only. So it ports self-contained (no third_party submodule). The port keeps the capture directory numbering (19) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (this list's number 20 is BYOL -- see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning
paper.authors: Grill, Strub, Altche, Tallec, Richemond, Buchatskaya, Doersch, Pires, Guo, Azar, Piot, Kavukcuoglu, Munos, Valko

scope: The paper-faithful ResNet-50 path is ported: an online network (ResNet-50 backbone -> projection MLP 2048->4096->256 -> prediction MLP 256->4096->256) is trained so its prediction of one view matches a target network's projection of the other; the target is an EMA copy of the online backbone + projector (no predictor, no gradient), updated each step with a cosine-scheduled momentum tau (0.996 -> 1.0). The loss is a symmetric negative cosine similarity with a stop-gradient on the target -- NO negatives, NO queue. Two views use the asymmetric BYOL augmentation (view1 strong blur; view2 weak blur + solarize). Optimised with LARS under a cosine LR schedule with warmup. The capture's unified Step 2 (models/vit_byol.py, arch: vit) is also ported additively: the same ViT-B/16 backbone every method shares as the BYOL online encoder, AdamW with batch-linear LR scaling + warmup/cosine, AMP on CUDA and gradient clipping, EMA tau 0.996 -> 1.0, milestone checkpoints at 100/200/300; the native ResNet-50 path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
encoder: encoder.pt is the online ResNet-50 backbone (online_encoder.*): the torchvision resnet50 up to and including avgpool, plus a Flatten, producing a 2048-d feature. The projection MLP (online_projector.*), the prediction MLP (predictor.*) and the entire target network (target_encoder.*, target_projector.*) are training machinery and are excluded -- the standard SSL convention of probing the backbone, the same shape as the mocov1/v2 ports.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the online ResNet-50 backbone (2048-d, avg-pooled) via encode(), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation -- the same normalisation BYOL trains with). Follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: the paper-faithful ResNet-50 path and the unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (arch: vit) are both ported; the ViT path (models/vit_byol.py, train_pretrain_vit_byol.py, configs/pretrain_vit.yaml) is port-authored from the capture's train_step2_vit.py + models/vit_byol.py, reuses the native ProjectionMLP/PredictionMLP/BYOLLoss and the two-view byol dataset, keeps AMP+grad-clip (as the capture's BYOL ViT loop does), and adds timm as a lazy dependency

the EMA target update, the symmetric negative-cosine loss with stop-gradient, the LARS optimizer and the cosine EMA-tau schedule are kept faithfully (all torch); tau is recomputed each step from the fractional epoch
the two-view dataset returns ((view1, view2), label); the asymmetric BYOL augmentation (view1 blur p=1.0; view2 blur p=0.1 + solarize p=0.2) is kept
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture called x.cuda())
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, the AMP autocast/GradScaler and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32; the cosine LR schedule with warmup and the batch-linear LR scaling are kept
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
